title: In vivo passive thoracolumbar axial rotation stiffness, seated with pelvis fixed, right vs left and male vs female

quantity.name: axial rotational stiffness
quantity.definition: slope of the linear regression of applied moment vs measured axial rotation (potentiometer on the shoulder-harness pulley) over 6 moment levels 3.7-22.0 Nm; shoulders rotated relative to the fixed pelvis/lower limbs (thoracolumbar spine incl. thorax)

source.authors: Kosmopoulos V, Lopez JA, McCain J, Kumar S

protocol.summary: Axial Rotation Tester (AROT): seated upright, lower extremities from the hips down fixed by four Velcro belts; a shoulder harness rigidly attached to an overhead pulley (35 cm diameter) loaded by a cable and dead weights to apply moments of 3.7, 7.3, 11.0, 14.7, 18.4 and 22.0 Nm bilaterally in random order; device minimises flexion/extension while allowing axial rotation and coupled lateral flexion.
how_to_simulate: Seated model, pelvis and lower limbs fixed; shoulder girdle/upper thorax rotated about the vertical spinal axis, flexion/extension constrained, lateral bending free
Apply axial moments of 3.7-22.0 Nm to the upper thorax and record the rotation relative to the pelvis; fit the slope (Nm/rad) and compare (both directions)

subject_model.source: Table 1 (mean of male and female means; derived)

protocol.notes: Rotation measured at the shoulders, so it includes thoracic and lumbar axial rotation (thoracolumbar). Linear fit R2 ~0.96. Watt 2022 used this study in its axial-rotation synthesis (values converted to Nm/deg). No EMG monitoring reported.
